Done. Both deliverables are in place at `out/纪要.docx` and `out/summary.json`, generated from the transcript only.

**How I handled the two recording defects:**

The transcript names five speakers — 刘文博, 黄静怡, 黄文博, 王晓雯, 张晓雯 — with no timestamps anywhere. Two pairs collide on a name element: 刘文博/黄文博 share 文博, and 王晓雯/张晓雯 share 晓雯. 黄静怡 also shares the surname 黄 with 黄文博, but her full name is unique. I treated the 文博 and 晓雯 speakers as the ambiguous ones and appended `（归属待核）` to exactly those five-entry attributions; 黄静怡's two entries carry no suffix because she is uniquely identifiable. I did not invent any 甲/乙/department markers to separate them.

**Content, all verbatim from the transcript:**

- 决议事项 (3): 刘文博 on the plan proceeding as originally scheduled, 黄静怡 on the 300万元 budget via 专项列支, 黄文博 on the new acceptance criteria superseding the old version.
- 待办事项 (4, as a 事项/负责人/期限 table): 黄静怡 finishing the 复盘纪要 by 6月30日前, 王晓雯 archiving the 灰度放量方案 by 7月中旬, 张晓雯 mapping out 责任分工, and 刘文博 sending the 验收清单 material to the group chat. The last two have no stated deadline, so their 期限 is `未明确`.
- 风险与关注 (2): 张晓雯 on the 市场部 fulfillment/积压 risk, 刘文博 on the unaligned 数据口径 and missing 基线数据.

`summary.json` records `{"决议事项": 3, "待办事项": 4, "风险与关注": 2, "合计": 9}`.

**Verification.** I re-opened the finished docx from disk and checked it independently of the generator: no `[HH:MM]` pattern anywhere, the three section headings verbatim and in order, table headers verbatim, every numbered entry matching the `N. 【类别 · 相关人】内容` shape with its content traceable as a literal substring of the transcript, every named person drawn from the speaker set, and the `（归属待核）` suffix present on exactly the ambiguous entries and absent from the unique one. All 18 checks passed. LibreOffice also converted the file to PDF without complaint, confirming it opens in a real word processor.

Two notes on judgment calls. The brief scopes the `（归属待核）` rule to numbered entries, and the table has 负责人 rather than a 相关人 field, so I left the table cells as plain verbatim text — the suffix convention lives only in the two numbered sections. And I stripped the sentence-final 。 from quoted lines, which the brief permits. I also left `build_minutes.py` in the working directory; it asserts every quoted fragment against the source text and aborts on any non-verbatim string, so it documents how the minutes were derived and can be re-run to reproduce them.
